pages.text: By LuV the air-cooled rack's 24 CWU/t no longer feeds a training line. The $(item)Liquid-Cooled Compute Rack$() packs the same optical compute supply into a 5×5×3 double-row cabinet: $(bold)four LuV liquid blades give exactly 64 CWU/t$().$(br2)That number has a purpose — the vanilla $(item)Research Station$() wants $(bold)32 CWU/t$() per recipe, so $(bold)one rack now drives it alone$() with no extra racks and no HPCA.

pages.title: The 5×5×3 Structure
pages.text: The liquid casing plinth carries the energy, fluid and maintenance hatches. Put a $(item)Datacenter Hardware Hatch$() in an exposed liquid casing cell and face its port outward. Load four blades and the optional snack there. The y=2 rear computer-casing row accepts up to two native transmitters for external optical links. The roof carries frames and grating.

pages.title: Coolant Is a Real Input
pages.text: A cold plate running on electricity alone is an illusion: while providing computation the rack drinks $(bold)1 mB$() of coolant per tick from its fluid input hatch.$(li)$(item)Distilled Water$(): efficiency 1.00, the simple choice.$(li)$(item)PCB Coolant$(): efficiency 0.85, another 15% off cooling power and a lower PUE.$(br2)With no coolant the rack grants a $(bold)20-tick$() grace window, then $(bold)drops to 0 CWU/t$() and labels the GUI "cold plates starved of coolant". Refilling restores it immediately — the derate is never sticky.

pages.title: PUE 1.20 and Two Hard Limits
pages.text: Room PUE settles as $(bold)total = IT draw + base cooling × environment × airflow × cold-plate efficiency$(). The liquid cabinet's base cooling ratio is only 0.20, so $(bold)a neutral room at full load is PUE 1.20$(); natural cold sources (snowy plains, frozen/deep ocean, $(bold)Y < 20$()) multiply by 0.6, while the Nether and hot deserts multiply by 2.0.$(br2)Two hard limits exist for the training cluster to check:$(li)$(#0E7490)Switch bandwidth$(): one rack hands out at most $(bold)64 CWU/t$() per tick; surplus requests queue instead of erroring.$(li)$(#0E7490)VRAM$(): $(bold)blades carry no memory since 0.6.1$() — cluster memory lives in the memory racks' HBM modules, see chapter 6.

pages.title: Strict Same-Tick Budget
pages.text: Same rules as the 0.3 air-cooled rack:$(li)Simulation queries only read; they never deduct.$(li)Real allocations share one tick window, so $(bold)a Research Station, a pretraining cluster and an offload node all compete for the same pool$() — nobody gets the same CWU/t twice.$(li)A soft-mallet pause, unfixed maintenance, no blades, low power or a dry cold plate all zero the output and name the reason in the GUI.
